This happens when you don't have the filesystem support installed

Your mistake was setting your partitions like they were permanent. Ext file systems are not really designed to be managed the way you wanted. This is where you originally messed up.

If you wanted to stick with an ext file system you should have done so in an lvm. Lvm lets you manage your partitions on the fly without needing to reboot or use a live CD. Though, I do not know of any graphical partition managers that fully support lvm management, using cli is quite easy.

If you don't want to redo your system to use lvm, you can use the gparted live CD. Boot off that and you will be able to adjust your partitions.

But, really, the question I have is, why not just keep your /home on its own partition, in an lvm, letting you just add storage whenever you see fit? Your / and /var partitions shouldn't need to be altered after your install unless you messed something up.

I recommend reading Arch Linux Beginner's Guide

Even if you don't use Arch the wiki is still a treasure trove of information.

A quick glance shows that you need to use different tools depending on what is already on your system. Not surprisingly all tools are all command line, it is Arch after all, they have unisex toilets for humans and robots.

If you want to shrink a Windows partition then you should absolutely do it from Windows. Using Linux-based partition managers often leads to destruction of files, at least from what I've heard. Use Partition Wizard to shrink your NTFS partition.
